fieldMarks: Broad tail nearly a foot long, brown with a white fringe; raised as a white 'flag' showing white underside and rump when fleeing.
Reddish coat in summer, grayish in winter.
Bucks' antlers have a forward-curving main beam with single points rising from it; roughly 1 doe in 1,000 grows small antlers.
behavior: Rut peaks in the last three weeks of November in Canada; bucks' necks swell and they travel almost constantly.
Gathers in winter 'deer yards' for food and shelter from deep snow.
Eats leafy plants, grasses, mushrooms and berries in summer; twigs, buds, acorns and waste grain in fall and winter.
Does leave nearly scentless spotted fawns hidden for hours.
habitat: Forest edges and mixed forest north into the boreal forest, and farmland mosaics.
range: Southern Canada from Cape Breton Island west to south-central British Columbia, north into the boreal forest, and south through the US.

lookalikes.name: Mule deer
lookalikes.howToTell: Mule deer have a small white tail with a black tip, larger ears and antlers that fork and re-fork.

lookalikes.name: Black-tailed deer
lookalikes.howToTell: Black-tailed deer occur only west of the Great Divide and flag with less flare.
